AI-Powered Social Listening
and Crisis Response
AeroMitra | A decision-support prototype for an Indian airline

Detect what may spread.
Ground the response. Keep a person accountable.
Educational prototype | AeroMitra is fictional | No response is published without human approval
The prototype turns a noisy social feed into a prioritised human work queue.
Airlines receive routine mentions, service complaints and a small number of posts that can become public incidents. Response capacity is limited.
An LLM classifies the post. A virality model estimates spread. Policy retrieval constrains the draft reply.
Use AI to prioritise and draft. Keep crisis escalation and public release with a human reviewer.
Educational prototype | AeroMitra is fictional | No response is published without human approval
The cost of a missed crisis is not the same as the cost of an unnecessary review.
Most mentions are routine. Manual teams cannot read every post with equal attention.
A missed safety, discrimination or legal issue can escalate before the brand reacts. A false alarm mainly consumes review time.
A fluent LLM reply can create new risk if it promises compensation, exposes booking details or invents policy.
Which posts deserve attention now, and what reply—if any—is safe to prepare?

ChromaDB retrieves relevant AeroMitra policies. The LLM drafts only within that context. A human Approve, Edit or Reject action is required.
The system recommends attention and prepares language. It does not publish on its own.

6,000 synthetic posts
4,841 train | 1,159 held-out test
Target: spread
Inputs: text, language, issue, sentiment, severity and synthetic account metadata
Outcome field retweets_24h excluded to prevent leakage

635 synthetic English, Hindi and Hinglish posts
Gold labels for sentiment, issue type, severity and escalation
Held-out evaluation sample protects against prompt tuning on the test set
A model result is useful only when the test set is untouched, the target is defined before training, and failure costs are explicit.
Limitation: the data is synthetic and should demonstrate the pipeline, not represent production airline behaviour.

Rent the foundation model. Build the decision layer and controls.

Enterprise social listening suite

Strength: mature integrations and support
Trade-off: less control over policy logic and cost

Hosted LLM and managed infrastructure

Strength: fast prototyping and variable cost
Trade-off: privacy, model availability and rate limits

AeroMitra decision layer

Strength: transparent thresholds, policy rules and approval workflow
Trade-off: maintenance and governance effort
Pilot with rented model capacity and a small internal review team. Scale only after real-data validation, privacy review, and evidence that alert quality improves response time.

Synthetic labels may not reflect real airline behaviour. Hinglish, sarcasm and language mixing can reduce model reliability.
False alarms consume PR capacity. Missed high-spread negative posts delay action. Spread is a proxy, not the same as a crisis.
A fluent reply can still hallucinate a promise or cite the wrong policy. Grounding and validation reduce, but do not eliminate, that risk.
Validate on real permitted data. Test across languages. Add access-controlled audit logs. Review privacy terms. Keep human approval for every public response.

Use AI to focus attention.
Keep accountability human.
AeroMitra demonstrates a practical operating model for social listening: detect, prioritise, ground, draft and review.
